clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the President's Advisory Board on Arms Proliferation Policy within the Department of Defense, with five members appointed by the President from private life and a Chairperson designated by the President. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13062, signed September 29, 1997, ends its lead-in with "have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 12946, establishing the President’s Advisory Board". Section 7 reads "Sec. 7. This order shall be effective September 30, 1997.", so the end is dated 1997-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the next line with the words "on Arms Proliferation Policy;".

Section 2 directs the Board to advise the President on implementation of United States conventional arms transfer policy and other arms proliferation matters, reporting through the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 12946 (60 FR 4829, PDF pages 1-2 of the 1995-01-24 issue; sha256 d82be5dd...), headed Executive Order 12946 of January 20, 1995, President’s Advisory Board on Arms Proliferation Policy, matching the census register row (1995-01-20). Text and inventory: eleven scopes cover sections 1 through 4(d) to the signature; I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory board. Ending: Executive Order 13062 section 3(c) revokes Executive Order 12946, effective September 30, 1997 (section 7). The report-relative termination in section 4(a) is not an end because no held source dates the President's submission of the final report to the Congress (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines). Original grade: Federal Register machine text.

savings.reason: Executive Order 13062 does not preserve the order. Agreements executed by Board members and staff under section 4(d) before the revocation, and the Board's completed work, are accrued acts that the revocation does not itself undo; section 4(d) itself says the duty not to reveal classified information is subject to what applicable law authorizes, and no held source says more about the agreements, so the continuing effect of any agreement is not decided here.
